ankle_pumps: Lie or sit with the leg straight.
Pull toes up towards you, then point them away.
Moves swelling out after injury or surgery.
quad_set: Sit or lie with the leg straight and a rolled towel under the knee.
Tighten the thigh to press the back of the knee into the towel.
Watch the kneecap glide up as the muscle switches on.
slr: Lie on your back, other knee bent.
Lock the straight knee with a quad set first.
Lift the leg to the height of the other knee, lower slowly.
If the knee bends during the lift (a 'lag'), go back to quad sets.
heel_slide: Slide the heel towards your bottom as far as comfortable.
Use a towel around the foot to help if needed.
prone_hang: Lie face down with the kneecap just off the end of the bed.
Full straightening early is one of the most important goals after ACL surgery.
patellar_mob: Sit with the leg straight and thigh relaxed.
Gently glide the kneecap up, down, in and out with your fingers.
Hold each direction a few seconds.
Only after surgery when your surgeon or physio has cleared it.
mini_squat: Feet hip-width, hold a support if needed.
Sit back a little as if to a high chair, knees to about 45°.
Push through both heels to stand.
Knees track over the 2nd toe, not caving in.
wall_sit: Back against a wall, slide down to a pain-free knee angle.
Isometric holds often reduce knee and tendon pain for a while afterwards.
spanish_squat: Loop a strong band behind both knees and anchor it to a post.
Lean back into the band and sit down until shins are vertical.
A go-to exercise for jumper's knee (patellar tendinopathy).
tke: Vastus medialis, last degrees of extension
Band around the back of the knee, anchored in front.
Start with the knee slightly bent.
Push the knee back to fully straight against the band, squeeze 2 s.
Slow and controlled, no snapping into lock.
step_up: Step up with the working leg and stand tall.
Step down slowly with the other leg.
Raise the step height as strength improves.
step_down: Stand on a step on the working leg.
Slowly lower the other heel to touch the floor in front.
Push back up without locking the knee hard.
Knee stays in line with the foot. Use a mirror.
split_squat: Long stride stance, back heel up.
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor.
Drive up through the front heel.
Front knee may go over the toes; keep it in line with the foot.
bulgarian: Back foot on a bench behind you.
Lower down on the front leg under control.
Drive up through the front foot.
Add dumbbells or a backpack when 3×10 is easy.
squat: Feet shoulder-width (hold a weight at the chest to progress).
Sit down between the heels to a pain-free depth.
3 s down, 3 s up builds strength in tendons too.
decline_squat: Stand on one leg on a 25° slope (decline board or wedge).
Use the other leg to help come back up if needed.
bridge: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Squeeze glutes and lift hips into a straight line.
Push through heels; don't arch the low back.
sl_bridge: Bridge position, lift one foot off the floor.
Hips stay level like a table.
clamshell: Lie on your side, knees bent, heels together.
Open the top knee without rolling the pelvis back.
Add a band above the knees for progression.
hip_abd: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent.
Lift the straight top leg slightly behind the body.
Strong hip abductors reduce knee 'caving in'.
sl_rdl: Stand on one leg with a soft knee.
Hinge forward, the free leg going back, back flat.
Return to standing by squeezing the glute.
Hold a wall at first. Hips stay square to the floor.
hip_hinge: Hold a stick along your spine touching head, upper back and tailbone.
Push the hips back, keeping all 3 contact points.
The safe way to bend and lift.
slider_curl: Lie on your back, heels on towels on a smooth floor.
Slide the heels out slowly, then pull them back in.
Start with two legs, progress to one.
nordic: Kneel with a partner holding your ankles.
Lower your body forward as slowly as possible, hips straight.
Catch yourself with your hands, push back up.
One of the best-proven hamstring injury preventers in football.
iso_ham: Lie on your back, knee bent at about 30°.
Dig the heel into the floor at low effort (30–50%).
Should feel like work, not pain.
strides: Reach the target speed in the middle third.
jog: Each pain-free session, add jog time.
Run on flat, even ground first.
bike: Seat high enough that the knee is almost straight at the bottom.
Rock back and forth first if a full turn is not yet possible.
walk: Walk on flat ground at a pace that raises breathing.
Keep posture tall and arms swinging.
For low back pain, walking is one of the best treatments.
pogo: Small quick hops on both feet, knees nearly straight.
Stay on the balls of the feet.
drop_land: Step off a low box (20–30 cm).
Land on both feet softly, hips back, knees over toes.
Quiet landings mean good shock absorption.
lateral_bound: Jump sideways from one leg to the other.
Land and stick for 2 s before the next.
Knee must not cave inward on landing.
sl_hop: Land softly and hold for 3 s.
Progress distance, then add lateral and diagonal hops.
Compare distance with the uninjured leg — target 90%+.
agility: Finally unplanned cuts reacting to a partner's signal.
Unplanned cutting is the last step before full training.
copenhagen: Side plank with the top leg on a bench.
Short lever: knee on the bench. Long lever: ankle on the bench.
Lift hips and hold, bottom leg free.
Shown to cut groin injuries in football by around 40%.
adductor_squeeze: Lie on your back, knees bent, ball or fist between the knees.
Increase squeeze effort as pain allows.
side_lunge: Shift to one side, bending that knee, other leg straight.
Keep the bent knee in line with the foot.
hip_flexor_stretch: Half-kneel, back knee on a cushion.
Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the back glute.
calf_raise: Stand on both feet, hold a support.
Rise high onto the balls of the feet.
Move to the edge of a step for more range.
sl_calf_raise: Stand on one foot, light hand support.
bent_knee_calf: Stand with knees bent about 30° (or seated with weight on the knees).
Rise onto the toes keeping the knee bend.
The soleus takes huge load when running.
iso_calf: Rise onto the toes halfway on one or two legs.
Helps settle Achilles pain before heavier loading.
eccentric_heel_drop: Stand on a step on the balls of both feet.
Shift onto the injured leg and lower the heel slowly over 3 s.
Use both legs to come back up.
Insertional (heel-bone) pain: don't drop below step level.
band_4way: Sit with a band around the forefoot.
Push down, pull up, turn in, turn out against the band.
Eversion (turning out) is the key one after a sprain.
ankle_abc: Sit with the foot off the floor.
Draw the alphabet with your big toe.
Move from the ankle, not the knee.
knee_to_wall: Face a wall, toes a few cm away.
Drive the knee to touch the wall, heel down.
Move the foot back as range improves.
Normal is about 10 cm toe-to-wall. Compare both sides.
calf_stretch: Hands on a wall, injured leg behind.
Then bend the back knee to stretch the soleus.
sl_balance: Stand on one leg, knee soft.
Progress: eyes closed → on a pillow → catching a ball.
Balance training reduces repeat ankle sprains.
star_reach: Reach the other foot forward, back-left, back-right as far as you can.
short_foot: Sit or stand with the foot flat.
Pull the ball of the foot towards the heel to raise the arch, toes relaxed.
towel_scrunch: Curl the toes to pull the towel towards you.
Spread the toes wide at the end.
Add a light weight on the towel later.
plantar_stretch: Sit and cross the leg over the other knee.
Pull the toes back towards the shin.
Feel a stretch in the arch.
Do this before your first steps in the morning.
ball_roll: Roll the arch over a ball or frozen water bottle.
A frozen bottle also helps calm pain.
rathleff: Single-leg heel raise: 3 s up, 2 s hold, 3 s down.
Add a backpack with books as it gets easy.
tib_raise: Lean back against a wall, heels 30 cm away.
Lift the toes and forefoot towards the shins.
Strengthens the shin muscles that suffer in shin splints.
cat_camel: Slowly round the back up, then let it sag gently.
Mobility, not stretching. Keep it gentle.
dead_bug: On your back, arms up, hips and knees at 90°.
Lower opposite arm and leg slowly.
Keep the low back gently against the floor.
Breathe out as the limbs lower.
bird_dog: Reach opposite arm and leg out long.
Hold 5–10 s, don't rotate the hips.
Imagine a cup of tea on your lower back.
mcgill_curl: On your back, one knee bent, hands under the low back.
Lift head and shoulders just off the floor, neck still.
The low back stays in its natural curve.
side_plank: On your side, elbow under the shoulder.
Knees bent first, then straight legs.
Lift hips into a line and hold.
Head, hips, feet in one line.
open_book: Lie on your side, knees bent, arms together in front.
Open the top arm across to the other side, following it with your eyes.
kb_deadlift: Hinge at the hips, flat back, grab the handle.
Gradual loading builds a stronger, less sensitive back.
carry: Hold a heavy weight in one hand.
Walk tall for 20–30 m without leaning.
pendulum: Lean forward with a hand on a table.
Let the sore arm hang loose.
Make small circles by swaying your body.
Arm stays relaxed — the body moves it.
scap_squeeze: Draw shoulder blades back and down.
No shrugging up to the ears.
wall_slide: Forearms on a wall, elbows at shoulder height.
Slide arms up the wall in a pain-free range.
Stop below the point of pain.
er_band: Elbow at your side, towel under it, band in hand.
ir_band: Elbow at your side, band anchored to the outside.
Rotate the forearm in towards the belly.
pull_apart: Hold a band at shoulder height, arms straight.
Pull the band apart to touch the chest.
Ribs down, don't arch the back.
wall_pushup: Hands on a wall at shoulder height, body straight.
Bend the elbows to bring the chest to the wall.
Push back, then push a little further to spread the shoulder blades.
The 'plus' at the end protects the shoulder.
db_press: Sit or stand with light dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press up in a pain-free arc.
Start light; pain should stay 3/10 or lower.
wrist_iso: Forearm on a table, palm down, hand off the edge.
Push the back of the hand up against your other hand.
ecc_wrist: Forearm on a table, palm down, light dumbbell.
Use the other hand to lift the wrist up.
Mild discomfort is OK; sharp pain is not.
pron_sup: Hold a hammer by the handle, elbow at 90°.
Slowly rotate palm up then palm down.
Hold lower on the handle to make it easier.
grip: Squeeze a soft ball or towel.
Squeeze with the elbow straight later in rehab.
forearm_stretch: Arm straight in front, palm down.
Gently bend the wrist down with the other hand.
pushup: Hands under shoulders, body in a straight line (knees down to make it easier).
Lower the chest towards the floor.
Push back up without the hips sagging.
Too hard? Start with wall push-ups.
plank: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Lift into a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze glutes; don't let the hips sag.
superman: Lift arms, chest and legs slightly off the floor.
Small lift is enough — no cranking the neck.
jumping_jack: Jump the feet wide while raising the arms overhead.
Low-impact version: step one foot out at a time.
march: Lift one knee to hip height, then the other.
reverse_lunge: Step one foot back and lower the back knee towards the floor.
Push through the front heel to return.
Easier on the knees than forward lunges.
sit_to_stand: Sit on the front of a chair, feet flat.
Lean forward and stand up without using your hands.
The most useful leg exercise for daily life.
mountain_climber: High plank position, hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee towards the chest, then switch.
Slow it down to make it a core exercise.
neck_mob: Slowly nod down and up, then turn left and right.
Great break from phone and desk work.
chest_stretch: Forearm on a door frame, elbow at shoulder height.
Step through gently until you feel the chest stretch.
ham_stretch: Lie on your back with a towel around one foot.
Lift the straight leg until you feel a stretch.
Keep the other leg flat or bent — whatever is comfortable.
arm_circles: Make slow circles forward, then backward.
Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.
sl_squat: Stand on one leg in front of a box or chair.
Slowly sit back until you lightly touch the box.
Stand up on the same leg, knee in line with the 2nd toe.
Use a higher box to make it easier.
monster_walk: Band around the knees or ankles, knees slightly bent.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Toes point forward; don't let the knees cave in.
leg_ext: Straighten one knee fully and squeeze the thigh for 2 s.
Add an ankle weight to progress. After ACL surgery, ask your surgeon when this is allowed.
heel_walk: Lift the toes and walk on your heels.
Keep the knees straight and stand tall.
toe_walk: Rise high onto the balls of your feet.
Walk forward without letting the heels drop.
Keep the ankles straight, not rolling out.
quad_stretch: Bend the top knee and hold the ankle.
Pull the heel towards your bottom, keeping the knees together.
Push the hip slightly forward to feel more stretch.
chin_tuck: Sit or stand tall, eyes level.
Glide the chin straight back (make a 'double chin').
Don't nod down — slide straight back.
neck_iso: Place your hand against the side of your head.
Gently push the head into the hand without moving.
Hold 5–10 s. Repeat front, back and both sides.
band_row: Hinge forward with a flat back, weights or band in hands.
Pull the elbows back, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Keep the neck long and the back flat.
prone_y: Lie face down on a bench or the floor.
Lift the arms out to a 'T', then up to a 'Y', thumbs up.
side_er: Lie on your side, towel under the top elbow, elbow bent 90°.
Rotate the forearm up towards the ceiling.
One of the best-studied rotator cuff exercises.
press_up: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders.
Push the chest up, keeping the hips on the floor.
Helpful when bending forward hurts; stop if leg pain increases.
knee_to_chest: Pull one knee to your chest with both hands.
Breathe out and relax the back.
child_pose: Kneel and sit back towards your heels.
Reach the arms forward on the floor.
Relax and breathe into the back.
A cushion between heels and bottom helps if knees are stiff.
pallof_press: Stand side-on to a band anchored at chest height.
Hold the band at your chest, then press it straight out.
Hold 2 s without twisting, bring it back.
The trunk must not rotate towards the anchor.
bridge_march: Lift one foot a little off the floor, then the other.
Keep the hips level the whole time.
If the hips drop, go back to normal bridges.
side_add: Lie on your side, top leg bent in front.
Lift the straight bottom leg up off the floor.
toe_yoga: Lift only the big toe, keeping the others down.
Then lift the other four, keeping the big toe down.
Hard at first — it improves quickly.
glute_kickback: Kick one heel back and up to hip height.
Lower slowly without arching the back.
Squeeze the glute at the top.
hip_circles: Stand on one leg, hold a support.
Lift the other knee and draw big circles with it.
lateral_hop: Hop sideways over a line and land softly.
box_jump: Stand in front of a low box.
Swing the arms and jump onto the box, landing softly.
Land in a quiet half-squat, knees out.
skipping: Skip forward driving one knee up.
Land on the ball of the foot.
Swing the arms opposite to the legs.
Great warm-up before running and sprinting.
nerve_glide: Straighten the knee while lifting the head to look up.
Bend the knee while dropping the chin. Move slowly in rhythm.
Gentle movement only — a mild pull is fine, it should not increase leg pain afterwards.
thoracic_ext: Sit on a chair, hands behind your head.
Gently arch the upper back over the chair back, looking up.
Move from the upper back, not the low back.

scalp_massage: Place your fingertips (not nails) on the scalp.
Press firmly and move the skin in small circles — do not just rub the hair.
Work from the front hairline to the crown, the sides and the back of the head.
Keep going for the full time, breathing slowly.
Do it every day — results in studies took about 6 months.
neck_release: Tension around the head and neck
Sit tall and drop your shoulders.
Tilt your ear towards one shoulder and hold.
Gently press the tight muscle at the top of the shoulder with the other hand. Switch sides.
cheek_lift: Open your mouth into a long "O", lips covering the teeth.
Smile with the upper cheeks to lift them up.
Place your fingers lightly on the cheeks and hold, then relax.
jaw_relax: Rest the tip of your tongue behind the top teeth.
Slowly open your mouth as far as is comfortable, keeping the tongue there.
Close slowly. Then massage the jaw muscle in front of the ear in circles.
Stop if the jaw clicks painfully.
brow_smooth: Place your fingertips flat on the forehead.
Gently glide them out towards the temples, smoothing the skin.
Relax the eyebrows completely between strokes.
Use a little moisturiser so the fingers glide.
chin_lift: Sit tall and look up towards the ceiling.
Push your lower lip over the upper lip (or press the tongue to the roof of the mouth).
Feel the front of the neck work. Hold, then return slowly.
Skip it if looking up makes you dizzy.
smile_hold: Smile widely with the lips closed.
Pull the corners of the mouth up and back. Hold.
A real smile also makes you look more approachable.
eye_focus: Hold your thumb about 25 cm in front of your face.
Focus on it for a few seconds.
Then focus on something far away (6 m or more). Switch back and forth.
Blink normally — screens make us blink less.
eye_circles: Look up, down, left and right slowly, pausing at each end.
Then draw slow circles with your eyes, both directions.
Gentle — stop if it causes dizziness.
eye_palming: Rub your palms together to warm them.
Cup them over your closed eyes without pressing.
Breathe slowly and enjoy the darkness.
brush_teeth: Brush all surfaces of the teeth for 2 minutes with fluoride toothpaste.
Brush gently along the gum line in small circles.
Clean between the teeth with floss or small brushes. Spit, don't rinse.
Brush your tongue too for fresh breath.
belly_breath: Sit or lie comfortably, one hand on the chest, one on the belly.
Breathe in through the nose for 4 seconds — only the belly hand rises.
Breathe out slowly through the mouth for 6 seconds.
A longer out-breath calms the body.
box_breath: Breathe in through the nose for 4 seconds.
Breathe out for 4 seconds, then hold for 4 seconds. Repeat.
Use it before an exam, an interview or sleep.
kegel: Sit or lie comfortably. Find the muscles you would use to stop passing urine and wind.
Squeeze and lift them inwards. Hold for the count, breathing normally.
Relax fully for the same time. Then do 10 quick squeezes.
Don't squeeze the buttocks or hold your breath. Don't practise while actually urinating.
finger_spread: Make a tight fist and hold for 2 seconds.
Open and spread the fingers as wide as you can.
Touch each fingertip to the thumb in turn.
Squeeze a soft ball or rolled towel to make it harder.
wrist_circles: Make slow circles with both wrists, 10 each way.
Hold one arm straight, palm up, and gently pull the fingers back.
Then palm down and pull the hand down. Switch arms.
Good for phone and computer users.
toe_spread: Sit with bare feet flat on the floor.
Spread all your toes as wide as possible and hold.
Relax, then lift all toes up while the ball of the foot stays down.
Use your hands to help at first.
knee_pushup: Kneel with hands under the shoulders.
Keep a straight line from knees to head.
Lower the chest towards the floor, then push back up.
When 3 × 12 is easy, try full push-ups.
pike_pushup: Start in a push-up position and walk your feet in so the hips go up into an upside-down V.
Bend the elbows and lower the top of the head towards the floor.
Shorter range is fine at first.
chair_dip: Sit on the edge of a stable chair, hands next to your hips.
Slide your bottom off the chair, knees bent.
Bend the elbows to lower yourself a little, then push back up.
Keep the shoulders down; stop if the front of the shoulder hurts.
sumo_squat: Stand with feet wide, toes turned out.
Sit down between your heels with the chest up.
Push through the heels to stand and squeeze the glutes.
Knees follow the line of the toes.
fire_hydrant: On hands and knees, back flat.
Lift one bent knee out to the side to hip height.
Lower slowly. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
Don't lean away — keep the hips level.
high_knees: Run on the spot, lifting the knees to hip height.
Land softly on the balls of the feet.
burpee: Squat down and put your hands on the floor.
Step or jump the feet back to a plank, then bring them back in.
Stand up and reach the arms overhead (add a small jump if you can).
Step back instead of jumping to make it easier.
leg_raise: Lie on your back, hands under your lower back or by your sides.
Keep the low back pressed down and lift both legs up.
Lower them slowly without the back arching.
Bend the knees to make it easier.
progress_photo: Take a photo in the same place and light each week (front and side).
Optional: measure your waist at the belly button.
Compare month to month, not day to day.
Photos stay in your own phone gallery — the app never sees them.
bottle_press: Hold two filled water bottles (or a light backpack) at shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and press them straight up.
Lower slowly back to the shoulders.
Don't arch the lower back — ribs stay down.
backpack_row: Put books or water bottles in a backpack and hold it by the top handle.
Hinge forward with a flat back, the other hand on a chair.
Pull the elbow back towards the hip, then lower slowly.
Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top. Do both sides.
band_press: Stand on the middle of a band, ends in your hands at shoulder height.
Stand with feet wider for more tension.
step_jack: Stand tall, arms by your sides.
Step one foot out to the side while raising both arms overhead.
Step back in and repeat on the other side. Keep a quick rhythm.
Good for flats — no noise for the neighbours.
slow_burpee: Squat down and put your hands on the floor.
Step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Step the feet back in and stand up tall.
Move steadily — quiet but still hard work.

PLANS.name: Head-to-Toe Daily
PLANS.tag: Free · about 20 min a day · everyone
PLANS.desc: A short daily routine that looks after everything from your scalp to your toenails: hair, face, eyes, posture, a quick full-body workout, feet and healthy habits.

PLANS.name: Men: Strong, Lean & Confident
PLANS.desc: Build broad shoulders, a strong back and chest, powerful legs and a firm waist — at home, with little equipment. Includes the daily head-to-toe care routine and habits for skin, hair and sleep.

PLANS.name: Women: Toned, Strong & Glowing
PLANS.desc: Shape strong glutes and legs, a defined waist, toned arms and upright posture — at home, at your own pace. Includes the daily head-to-toe care routine and habits for skin, hair and sleep.

PLANS.name: Hair & Scalp Care
PLANS.tag: Men & women · 30 days · 7 min + a walk
PLANS.desc: Daily scalp massage, stress-lowering breathing, neck release, a brisk walk and the food and care habits that support healthy hair. Honest note: no exercise can reverse genetic hair loss — this plan supports your hair and tells you when to see a doctor.

PLANS.name: Face, Neck & Posture
PLANS.desc: Stand taller and look fresher: face and jaw exercises, eye breaks, neck and upper-back strength, plus sun protection and sleep habits.

HAB.water: Drink water through the day (about 6–8 glasses)
HAB.protein: Protein with every meal (eggs, meat, fish, beans, dairy)
HAB.sun: Sunscreen SPF 30+ on face and neck
HAB.teeth: Brush teeth morning and night (2 min)
HAB.ironfood: Iron & zinc foods today (meat, eggs, lentils, greens, nuts)
HAB.gentlehair: No tight hairstyles or very hot dryer today
HAB.posture: Posture check every hour: chin back, shoulders down

uz.Exercise cannot reverse genetic (pattern: Mashq irsiy (androgen) soch to‘kilishini to‘xtata olmaydi. Lekin u sog‘lom sochni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi: stressni kamaytiradi, uyquni yaxshilaydi va qon aylanishini oshiradi.
uz.Daily scalp massage: in small studies, a: Har kuni bosh terisini uqalash: kichik tadqiqotlarda kuniga taxminan 4 daqiqa, 6 oy davomida sochni biroz qalinlashtirgan. Bu bepul va xavfsiz — muntazam bo‘ling.
uz.Eat enough protein, iron and zinc (meat,: Yetarli oqsil, temir va rux iste’mol qiling (go‘sht, tuxum, loviya, yasmiq, ko‘katlar). Keskin parhezlar ko‘pincha 2–3 oydan keyin soch to‘kilishiga sabab bo‘ladi.
uz.Be gentle: avoid tight ponytails, braids: Ehtiyot bo‘ling: tor bog‘langan dum, o‘rim va tugunlardan, juda issiq fen va kuchli kimyoviy vositalardan saqlaning.
uz.Proven treatments for pattern hair loss: Androgen soch to‘kilishining isbotlangan davolash usullari (masalan, minoksidil, erkaklarda finasterid) shifokor yoki farmatsevt maslahatini talab qiladi. Soch to‘satdan, o‘choq-o‘choq bo‘lib to‘kilsa yoki bosh terisi qichishib, po‘st tashlasa, shifokorga boring.
uz.Face exercises are a small, low-risk hab: Yuz mashqlari — kichik va xavfsiz odat. Bir kichik tadqiqotda 20 hafta davomida har kungi yuz mashqlari yonoqlarni biroz to‘liqroq ko‘rsatgan. Teri uchun eng muhimi — quyoshdan himoya, uyqu va chekmaslik.
uz.Relax the jaw during the day: teeth apar: Kun davomida jag‘ni bo‘shashtiring: tishlar ochiq, lablar yopiq, til tanglayga tegib turadi. Tishlarni qisish jag‘ og‘rig‘i va bosh og‘rig‘iga sabab bo‘lishi mumkin.
uz.Use the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes: 20-20-20 qoidasi: ekranga qaragan har 20 daqiqada 20 soniya davomida taxminan 6 metr uzoqlikdagi narsaga qarang.
uz.Eye exercises ease tiredness but do not: Ko‘z mashqlari charchoqni kamaytiradi, lekin yaqinni ko‘rishni tuzatmaydi. Kunduzi ochiq havoda vaqt o‘tkazish bolalar ko‘rishini himoya qiladi. Har 1–2 yilda ko‘zingizni tekshirtiring.
uz.Brush twice a day for 2 minutes with flu: Kuniga ikki marta 2 daqiqadan ftorli tish pastasi bilan tish yuving va kuniga bir marta tishlar orasini tozalang. Sog‘lom tabassum — eng jozibali narsalardan biri.
uz.Limit sugary drinks and snacks between m: Ovqatlar orasida shirin ichimlik va gazaklarni kamaytiring. Har 6–12 oyda stomatologga boring.
uz.Good posture is mostly strength and habi: Yaxshi qomat — asosan kuch va odat: kuchli yuqori orqa mushaklari, iyak biroz ichkariga, ekran ko‘z darajasida. Har 30–45 daqiqada holatingizni o‘zgartiring.
uz.Push-ups, rows and presses build strong: Otjimaniya, tortish va itarish mashqlari yelka va qo‘llarni kuchaytiradi. Ularni haftasiga 2–3 marta bajaring va takrorlarni asta-sekin oshiring.
